portfolio.title: Investment Club Portfolio
portfolio.subtitle: Stock Picks, Holdings Review & Recommendations
portfolio.week_narrative: Markets closed the first half of 2026 on a risk-on note as a U.S.-Iran resolution came into sight, easing the energy-price and flight-to-safety fears that dominated the spring. The S&P 500 (+1.61%) and Nasdaq (+2.38%) led gains, and JPMorgan hiked its 2026 S&P target to 7,800, implying another ~5% of upside. The cross-current is policy: Thursday's PCE report showed core inflation at 3.4% — a three-year high — and the Fed held at 3.50–3.75% on June 17 with Chair Warsh keeping a possible rate HIKE on the table. That combination (strong consumer + sticky inflation + Iran de-escalation + tariff/customs-enforcement escalation under the June 3 executive order) is rewarding broad index and quality-tech exposure while punishing the most leveraged, rate-sensitive bets — most visibly MSTR, which fell 9.3% on the week as Bitcoin cooled.

holdings.name: Strategy Inc
holdings.short_term_strategy: Do NOT add here. MSTR is sitting just above its 52-week low ($81.81) after a ~56% slide from its peak and a -9.3% week. Wait for Bitcoin to stabilize and the stock to reclaim and hold the $95–$100 zone on volume before considering any add. Hard mental stop / re-evaluation if it breaks below $81.81 on a weekly close. Q2 earnings on Aug 4 is a near-term volatility event — do not chase into it.
holdings.long_term_strategy: MSTR is a leveraged Bitcoin proxy holding ~847,000 BTC at a ~$75,650 average cost; the thesis is intact only if you remain structurally bullish on Bitcoin over 12–24 months. Crypto policy is turning supportive — the GENIUS Act is law and a state has launched a Bitcoin reserve — which favors institutional BTC adoption long term. Keep the position small as a high-beta satellite, and accumulate only via tiny DCA tranches on deep Bitcoin drawdowns rather than lump sums.
holdings.rationale: This week's macro backdrop — sticky 3.4% core PCE and a Fed signaling it may hike rather than cut — is precisely the higher-for-longer rate environment that punishes leveraged crypto bets like MSTR, explaining its -9.3% week. The HOLD reflects a still-constructive long-term crypto-policy tailwind (GENIUS Act, state Bitcoin reserves) against a hostile short-term rate and risk-appetite setup. Patience over panic-selling near the 52-week low.
holdings.cost_basis_note: Average cost basis is $323.04 vs. $85.34 — the position is deeply underwater (~-74%), roughly a $1,663 unrealized loss on 7 shares. Because the loss is already large and the long-term BTC thesis is unbroken, selling here crystallizes the worst-case; HOLD and let the thesis play out rather than capitulating at the low.

holdings.name: Netflix, Inc.
holdings.short_term_strategy: Hold into the July 16 Q2 earnings report — do NOT initiate covered calls (earnings within 3 weeks). NFLX is grinding just above its 52-week low ($70.86); a clean earnings beat could spark a relief rally toward $80–$85, while a miss risks a retest of the low. Consider adding a small tranche only after earnings clears the uncertainty and the stock holds above $75.
holdings.long_term_strategy: Netflix remains the streaming leader with strong cash flow and a fast-growing ad tier; analysts carry a Buy consensus with a ~$114 average target (well above current price). Its real-estate moves (reported Radford Studio purchase) and live-content push deepen the moat. Streaming faces limited near-term regulatory threat, making it a cleaner long-term compounder than the AI/crypto names — accumulate on post-earnings weakness for a 12–24 month hold.
holdings.rationale: With consumer spending still robust per this week's PCE data, Netflix's subscription + ad model is well positioned even as inflation pressures discretionary budgets. The HOLD is driven by the July 16 earnings catalyst landing inside the next three weeks — too close to add aggressively or to sell calls. The ~$114 analyst target frames meaningful long-term upside from a near-52-week-low entry.
holdings.cost_basis_note: Average cost basis is $110.63 vs. $72.72 — underwater ~-34% (~$379 unrealized loss on 10 shares). The single 2025 lot is well below breakeven, so the recommended action is to hold through earnings rather than sell at a loss; the gap to the analyst target supports patience.

holdings.name: NVIDIA Corporation
holdings.short_term_strategy: Accumulate on weakness between $185–$198. NVDA is consolidating below its 52-week high ($236.54) after a flat week, with semis broadly strong (Micron surged ~16% on earnings; SOX +3.2% that session). Add a tranche now and keep dry powder to buy a dip toward the $185 support shelf. Next earnings Aug 26 is the major catalyst — position before the late-summer run.
holdings.long_term_strategy: NVDA posted record Q1 FY27 revenue of $81.6B (+85% YoY) with Data Center +92% — the AI infrastructure buildout remains the dominant secular growth story, and analysts show 77 Buy vs. 1 Hold with an average target near $304. The key risk is policy: Senator Warren's June compliance inquiry and pending chip-export licensing rules could cap China revenue. Net-net, accumulate steadily; the structural AI demand outweighs the export-control overhang over 12–24 months.
holdings.rationale: This week's risk-on tape, Iran de-escalation, and blowout semiconductor earnings reinforce the AI capex super-cycle that drives NVDA. The BUY explicitly weighs that secular tailwind against a real political headwind — tightening U.S. chip-export rules and Warren's NVIDIA inquiry — which is why we add on dips rather than chase strength. With the stock below its high and earnings ahead, the risk/reward favors accumulation.
holdings.cost_basis_note: Average cost basis is $127.36 vs. $197.93 — the position is solidly profitable (~+55%, ~$423 unrealized gain on 6 shares). The healthy cushion lets us add to a winner with confidence and gives room to ride volatility into the Aug 26 earnings without threatening breakeven.

holdings.name: Vanguard S&P 500 ETF
holdings.short_term_strategy: Continue automatic dollar-cost averaging — no market timing needed. VOO is +1.62% on the week and just 2% below its 52-week high ($699.15) as the index pushes toward Wall Street's 7,800 S&P target. Keep buying on schedule; if a sticky-inflation scare triggers a 3–5% pullback, add an extra tranche near the $650 area.
holdings.long_term_strategy: VOO is the club's core engine — broad, low-cost S&P 500 exposure that compounds through cycles. Analysts see the S&P reaching 7,500–7,600+ by year-end, with bull cases above on AI-driven earnings. The structural rise in retail and Gen Z/Black investor participation supports steady inflows into index products. Maximize DRIP and keep contributing every cycle for the 12–24 month base and beyond.
holdings.rationale: An improving geopolitical picture (Iran resolution in sight) and resilient consumer spending underpin the broad market, even as the Fed's higher-for-longer stance caps the pace of gains. The BUY/keep-DCA call leans on the index's diversification to absorb the inflation and tariff cross-currents that whip individual names like MSTR. Dollar-cost averaging neutralizes the timing risk created by an uncertain rate path.
holdings.cost_basis_note: Average cost basis is $498.90 vs. $684.66 — profitable ~+37% (~$4,569 unrealized gain on 24.61 shares). The large cushion and core-holding role make continued accumulation the right move; this is the position to keep feeding every contribution cycle.

watchlist.name: Microsoft Corporation
watchlist.rationale: Microsoft sits near its 52-week low ($349.20) and well below the ~$561 average analyst target, even as Azure AI and Copilot adoption keep growing and operating margins run ~46.8%. A recent Xbox price hike weighed on sentiment, but the AI franchise is now larger than some legacy businesses. Watch for stabilization above $365 as a quality-on-sale entry.

watchlist.name: Meta Platforms, Inc.
watchlist.rationale: Meta is ~30% below its 52-week high ($796.25) amid AI-talent-departure and heavy capex concerns, with revenue still up ~22% YoY and an ~$841 average analyst target signaling large upside. The pullback is sentiment-driven, not fundamental. Monitor for a base near $520 (the 52-week low) before adding.

watchlist.name: Invesco QQQ Trust
watchlist.rationale: QQQ jumped +3.11% on the week and is pressing its 52-week high ($748.65) on renewed AI optimism and strong semis. It offers concentrated mega-cap tech exposure if the club wants more growth tilt than VOO. Watch for entries on pullbacks toward the $705 support rather than chasing the breakout.

watchlist.name: SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust
watchlist.rationale: DIA recently hit a fresh 52-week high and offers blue-chip value exposure (financials ~27%, industrials ~17%) that benefits from the rotation into cyclicals and small/value seen this week (Caterpillar +4% one session). It's a lower-volatility diversifier vs. the tech-heavy book. Consider as a defensive ballast if inflation forces a value rotation.

key_insights: Sticky 3.4% core PCE punishes leveraged MSTR; favors broad index VOO/QQQ
NVDA profitable +55% — accumulate dips into the Aug 26 earnings catalyst
Hold NFLX through July 16 earnings; no calls inside the window

strategies_to_adopt.strategy: Written investment thesis requirement (NAIC-style Stock Study lite)
steps: Create a 1-page template: ticker, thesis, 5-year growth, risks, price target, time horizon, cost-basis vs. price
Require submission 48 hours before any buy/sell vote
Archive every thesis in a shared Google Drive for quarterly review
Assign each member 1–2 sectors (Tech, Comm Services, Index/Macro, Crypto) to monitor monthly
Sector lead gives a 5-minute update each meeting tied to the week's macro/political news
Rotate assignments every 6 months for cross-training
Schedule a dedicated quarterly session separate from regular meetings
Review each holding against its original thesis AND current P/L vs. cost basis
Vote on rebalancing/trimming with full quorum (e.g., review the MSTR underwater thesis)

key_insights: Top clubs win on process, not picks — build the written-thesis framework first
ESG/community-values alignment is FI Community's strongest recruitment hook
Quarterly cost-basis reviews catch underwater theses like MSTR before they deepen

covered_calls.title: Covered Call Strategy
covered_calls.subtitle: Weekly Options Income on Club Holdings
covered_calls.market_iv_context: Implied volatility has cooled from the spring's geopolitical spike now that a U.S.-Iran resolution is in sight and indices are pressing record highs — broad-market IV (VOO/SPY) is on the lower end, while single names like MSTR and NVDA still carry elevated IV ahead of their August earnings. IMPORTANT: the club currently holds fewer than 100 shares of MSTR (7), NFLX (10) and NVDA (6), so single-contract covered calls are not yet executable on those names — the plays below are educational/positioning targets for when share counts reach 100, except where noted.
covered_calls.covered_call_primer: A covered call means selling someone the right to buy 100 of your shares at a set strike by a set date. You collect the premium today no matter what. If the stock stays below the strike, you keep the shares and the full premium. If it rises above the strike, your shares get called away at that price — you still profit, just capped at the strike. You must own at least 100 shares per contract.

plays.upcoming_catalyst: No earnings; macro events only (July 2 jobs report, ongoing inflation prints)

plays.watch_for: Once VOO holdings reach 100 shares, sell the ~$705 call ~35–40 DTE for ~$550 premium (~7.7% annualized) in any low-IV, range-bound stretch.

plays.name: NVIDIA Corporation

plays.historical_win_rate: NVDA calls at 5–8% OTM expire worthless a majority of the time outside earnings windows, but elevated IV makes outcomes wider.
plays.skip_reason: Two blockers: (1) the club owns only 6 NVDA shares, far below 100; and (2) NVDA is a BUY-and-accumulate name we don't want capped — selling calls would cut off upside in our most profitable position (+55%). A pre-Aug-26 expiry also risks IV crush around earnings.
plays.watch_for: Revisit only if the club ever reaches 100 NVDA shares AND shifts to an income posture. The best entry is typically the week AFTER the Aug 26 earnings once IV crushes and a new range forms.

plays.name: Strategy Inc
plays.upcoming_catalyst: Q2 2026 earnings on Aug 4, 2026 — a 25–45 DTE covered call would span the report
plays.skip_reason: Three blockers: (1) the club owns only 7 MSTR shares; (2) Aug 4 earnings falls inside any 25–45 DTE window — never sell calls within ~3 weeks of earnings; and (3) at $85 vs. a $323 cost basis, any strike near a realistic OTM level sits far below breakeven, so assignment would lock in a large loss.
plays.watch_for: Not a covered-call candidate while underwater. Re-evaluate only if/when MSTR recovers above the ~$323 cost basis with 100+ shares held — then high IV could fund attractive premiums.

Skip NFLX on the rule: July 16 earnings is inside the 3-week window

Prioritize the high-traffic finance/entrepreneurship events (Invest Fest, real estate meetups) for member recruitment and partner deals. Follow up on LinkedIn within 48 hours of every event.
